title: Angles and shapes
description: Animated KS3 Maths lesson on angles and shapes for ages 9 to 14: acute, obtuse and reflex angles, angles on a line, round a point and in a triangle, vertically opposite, alternate, corresponding and co-interior angles, polygons and the properties of 2D and 3D shapes.
intro: Types of angle, the angle rules, parallel lines, polygons and the properties of shapes, explained by the owl in five short parts.

steps.say: An **angle** measures a turn. We measure angles in **degrees**, written °. One full turn is 360°.
steps.speak: An angle measures a turn. We measure angles in degrees, written with a little circle. One full turn is 360 degrees.

steps.say: A **right angle** is a quarter turn: exactly 90°. We mark it with a little square.
steps.speak: A right angle is a quarter turn: exactly 90 degrees. We mark it with a little square.

steps.say: An **acute** angle is less than 90°. An **obtuse** angle is more than 90° but less than 180°.
steps.speak: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees. An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.

steps.say: A straight line makes an angle of 180°. A **reflex** angle is more than 180° but less than 360°.
steps.speak: A straight line makes an angle of 180 degrees. A reflex angle is more than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees.

check.hint: Is 210° more or less than a straight line, 180°?
check.explain: 210° is more than 180° and less than 360°, so it is a **reflex** angle.

steps.say: Angles on a **straight line** add up to 180°. One angle is 115°, so the other is x = 180° − 115° = 65°.
steps.speak: Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees. One angle is 115 degrees, so the other is x equals 180 minus 115, which is 65 degrees.

steps.say: Angles **round a point** add up to 360°. 100° + 140° = 240°, so y = 360° − 240° = 120°.
steps.speak: Angles round a point add up to 360 degrees. 100 plus 140 is 240 degrees, so y equals 360 minus 240, which is 120 degrees.

steps.say: The angles in a **triangle** add up to 180°. 40° + 75° = 115°, so x = 180° − 115° = 65°.
steps.speak: The angles in a triangle add up to 180 degrees. 40 plus 75 is 115 degrees, so x equals 180 minus 115, which is 65 degrees.

steps.say: The angles in a **quadrilateral** add up to 360°. Why? Cut it into two triangles: 2 × 180° = 360°.
steps.speak: The angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees. Why? Cut it into two triangles: 2 times 180 is 360 degrees.

check.q: Two angles in a triangle are 45° and 85°. What is the third angle?
check.hint: The three angles in a triangle add up to 180°. Add the two you know first.

steps.say: When two straight lines cross, the angles opposite each other are equal. They are called **vertically opposite** angles.
**Parallel** lines go in the same direction and never meet, like train tracks. We mark them with little arrows.
Draw a line across two parallel lines. The angles inside a **Z** shape are **alternate angles**. Alternate angles are equal.
The angles in an **F** shape are **corresponding angles**. They are equal too.
The angles inside a **C** or **U** shape are **co-interior angles**. They add up to 180°: 55° + 125° = 180°.
steps.speak: The angles inside a C or U shape are co-interior angles. They add up to 180 degrees: 55 plus 125 is 180 degrees.

check.q: A line crosses two parallel lines. One angle is 65°. What is the angle alternate to it?
check.hint: Look for the Z shape. Are alternate angles equal, or do they add up to 180°?
check.explain: Alternate angles are **equal**, so it is also **65°**.

steps.say: A **polygon** is a flat shape with straight sides. A triangle has 3 sides, a quadrilateral 4, a pentagon 5, a hexagon 6 and an octagon 8.
In a **regular** polygon, all the sides are the same length and all the angles are the same size.
The angles inside a hexagon add up to 720°. A regular hexagon has 6 equal angles, so each one is 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.
steps.speak: The angles inside a hexagon add up to 720 degrees. A regular hexagon has 6 equal angles, so each one is 720 divided by 6, which is 120 degrees.

steps.say: Walk all the way round a polygon and you make one full turn. So the **exterior angles** add up to 360°. Each exterior angle of a regular hexagon is 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.
steps.speak: Walk all the way round a polygon and you make one full turn. So the exterior angles add up to 360 degrees. Each exterior angle of a regular hexagon is 360 divided by 6, which is 60 degrees.

steps.say: An interior angle and its exterior angle sit on a straight line, so they add up to 180°: 120° + 60° = 180°.
steps.speak: An interior angle and its exterior angle sit on a straight line, so they add up to 180 degrees: 120 plus 60 is 180 degrees.

check.q: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular octagon?
check.hint: An octagon has 8 sides. The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°.

steps.say: Triangles: an **equilateral** triangle has 3 equal sides, an **isosceles** triangle has 2 equal sides, and a **scalene** triangle has no equal sides.
A **square** has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. A **rectangle** has 4 right angles. A **rhombus** has 4 equal sides, like a square pushed over.
A **parallelogram** has two pairs of parallel sides. A **trapezium** has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
A **line of symmetry** is a mirror line: fold along it and the two halves match. A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle has 2.
3D shapes have **faces**, **edges** and **vertices** (corners). A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices.

check.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
check.hint: Try folding from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
check.explain: You can fold an equilateral triangle in half from each of its 3 corners, so it has **3** lines of symmetry.
